questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Australia so I was excited for the opportunity to study in Sydney

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sydney is a great city to live in, but there was a lot of issues with my visa and the university experience was a lot different than what I had imagined. The academic level in classes suffered a lot from the high percentage of chinese students, that did not speak english. That meant that a lot of the time I was left alone in class discussions.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright. I had a hard time getting help with my visa situation, and the host university was not very helpful. Also there was a lot of bureaucracy from both the university and the government.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much really.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was not made aware of which visa stream to apply for, which resulted in me choosing the 'higher education' stream, rather than the 'awards sector', which I still don't know what is. Therefore, I almost didn't get my visa in time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was alright

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really expensive to live in Sydney

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was my experience that the level of the courses was a easier than at KU. It might just be the courses that I had. But it was really frustrating that not many of the students spoke english at a english university. It greatly affected the classes. I had a course where we were about 30 students, and I was the only non-chinese. Most of them did not really speak english. It was hard to get any class discussion going.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More participation is expected

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AMST1001 - Global America, EDUH4058 - Sport and Learning in Australian Culture, FILM1001 - Hollywood: Art, Industry, Entertainment, WRIT1000 - Introduction to Academic Writing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AMST1001 was great and had a very good lecturer. It was also really interesting because of the recent election. EDUH4058 was fun and easy.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The beach, explore the different suburbs, walk the coastal track

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the blue mountains, visit the markets, walk some of the coastal tracks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy in the city, but at university it was different. Might as well have studied in Shanghai, because it was not english spoken in the corridors, but mandarin.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There really isn't many. It is mostly international students, primarily from Asia

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. Meaning chinese.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are really friendly in Australia

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sydney is great. It is expensive. The university experience won't be an Australian one.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very careful with your visa application. The bureaucracy is crazy

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Sydney

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the governments visa bureaucracy
